about: Eric Hecker is a partner of Wang Hecker LLP, located in New York City, New York, where he represents clients in a wide variety of legal matters. His practice covers civil rights and business litigation, allowing him to advocate effectively for individuals and entities facing high-stakes challenges. Drawing on decades of elite legal experience, he is committed to providing meticulous preparation and practical solutions tailored to the unique needs of each client.

Mr. Hecker handles complex civil rights matters, including employment discrimination, police misconduct, prisoners' rights, and housing discrimination, helping clients navigate challenging disputes with clear legal counsel. His business litigation practice includes representing individuals and corporations involved in complex commercial disputes, contract issues, and partnership disagreements. In addition, he maintains an active appellate and trial practice, leveraging his extensive background to secure favorable outcomes in federal and state courts.

Admitted to practice in New York in 1999, Mr. Hecker is also admitted before the Supreme Court of the United States, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 2nd Circuit, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia and the U.S. District Courts for the Southern, Eastern, Northern and Western Districts of New York. Throughout his career, he has built a reputation for exceptional advocacy, emphasizing responsive communication and rigorous legal analysis designed to achieve impactful results.

Prior to entering private practice, Mr. Hecker distinguished himself through a series of prestigious judicial clerkships. He served as a law clerk for the Honorable Thelton Henderson of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California from 1997 to 1998, for the Honorable David Tatel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit from 1998 to 1999, and for the Honorable Constance Baker Motley of the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York from 2001 to 2002.

Mr. Hecker earned his Juris Doctor magna cum laude from the University of Michigan Law School in 1997. During his time at law school, he was elected to the Order of the Coif and served as articles editor of the Michigan Law Review. Before attending law school, he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Pennsylvania in 1991. Active in the legal and academic communities, he has also shared his knowledge as an adjunct professor, teaching election law at the Cardozo School of Law.
